Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the routing options you showed. We’re ready to lock a mutual action plan (MAP) so we can land a pilot and then a production rollout. Before we finalize timelines, two things we need clarified:

1) Hosting mode recommendation — our security team is leaning toward Dedicated because of PHI controls, but our product leadership wants to evaluate Hosted first to reduce ops burden. We need explicit risk/benefit tradeoffs and a recommended acceptance criteria if we start with Hosted.

2) Region and data residency — primary users will be in the US, but we have EU patient cohorts later this year. Can we get a clear path for US-only now and an add-on for EU West by Q4?

I’d appreciate a short MAP draft with the telemetry/SLAs and a proposed decision deadline for mode/region. Want to get this onto our procurement calendar for June.

Best,

Joanna — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a MAP draft (v3) plus a concise hosting-comparison matrix that lays out the acceptance criteria we typically use when customers evaluate Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private. High level answers below and I’ve called out decision checkpoints so procurement can schedule contract review: 

- Recommendation: Start with a Hosted pilot (90 days) scoped to a limited production path (US-only, controlled dataset) to validate latency and integration. Reason: fastest time-to-value, lower upfront cost.
- Fallback / escalation: If security gating requires isolation, we’ll transition to Dedicated. Acceptance criteria for transition are: PHI scope expands beyond the pilot bounds OR security audit flags that cannot be mitigated with contractual controls.
- Regional plan: US-East deployment for pilot (meets your latency targets). EU West option is available as an add-on; expected lead time 8–10 weeks from commitment.
- KPIs & gates in MAP: latency p50/p95, token spend per call, model output quality (sample prompt set pass rate), and audit-log availability.

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) MAP signoff & SOW redline (target: 2027-06-10)
2) Provision Hosted pilot (US-East) and credentials (target: 2027-06-17)
3) Pilot validation & quality gate (30 days) (target window: 2027-06-18 → 2027-07-18)
4) Decide on long-term mode (Hosted continue / move to Dedicated) (decision deadline: 2027-07-20)

I’ve attached: MAP_HealthStride_v3.pdf and hosting_comparison_matrix.xlsx. We’re flexible on the 90-day pilot length if you prefer a shorter acceptance window.

Next steps: Can you confirm procurement’s preferred date for the SOW redline review? We’ll loop in Legal (Laura) and Karthik for the technical cutover plan.

Thanks — Soojin

Adding technical context from infra/solutions: quick notes for the MAP so expectations are clear.

- Hosted pilot (US-East): we can guarantee isolation at the tenant level, token-level audit logs, and a dedicated routing profile to limit co-tenancy exposure. However, dedicated physical hardware (Dedicated) gives you HSM integration options and stricter network isolation (VPC) required by some auditors.
- Migration path: KV/cache export & model pinning will make a move from Hosted -> Dedicated straightforward for inference state — estimated cutover work 2–4 engineer-weeks (no model retrain).
- EU West add-on: operational lead time includes infra provisioning, compliance review (data transfer documentation), and an updated SOW for cross-border processing. 8–10 weeks estimate assumes no bespoke compliance artifacts are required.

Action items for the MAP: add a small tech appendix that lists the cutover checklist + expected engineering lead time. I’ve included a short excerpt from our SLA that matters for the pilot (redwood-sla-excerpt.pdf).

— Karthik
